lead: Former factories turning into a neighbourhood, with Jean Nouvel's Parc del Centre del Poblenou.
text: It is a neighbourhood whose boundaries were set in 2006; before that it was part of the traditional Poblenou. Its industrial zone was the "economic engine" of Poblenou in the last century, and the old factories are being turned into modern blocks. Its facilities include the former Can Ricart textile-printing factory, on Carrer d'Emília Coranty, with works under way as part of the 22@, and the Oliva Artés space of the Museu d'Història de Barcelona, in the Parc Central.

It combines the former industrial area with pockets of housing and a residential area. The Parc del Centre del Poblenou, designed by Jean Nouvel and opened in 2008 between Avinguda Diagonal and Carrer de Pere IV, is its great green space. The blocks from the 1970s face the Gran Via and the newer buildings face the Diagonal. If you are selling, the average sale price (4,234 €/m² in 2025) is practically in line with the Sant Martí average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 339,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Sant Martí (6th of 10 by price). If you are investing, the average rent (1,115 €/month) is in line with the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Blocks from the 1970s along the Gran Via and new-build on former factory sites, towards the Diagonal.
